entries.clue: Jocose friend trashed United (6,6)

indicators.note: something trashed is wrecked, so its letters are smashed up and rebuilt

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 12 letters

annotation.surface: A jokey pal has been rubbishing a football team called United.
annotation.walkthrough: United looks like the name of a football club being trashed, but it is the definition at the end, read as a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: To join forces is to unite, so 'joined forces' swaps for 'united'.

entries.clue: Taking some cover, Biden poorly estimated risk (7)

indicators.note: only part of the following words is taken, so the answer sits inside them

blocks.note: the letters run from the second letter of cover across the gap into the first three of Biden

annotation.surface: President Biden, taking cover, misjudged how dangerous something was.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma between 'cover' and 'Biden' is ignored; the answer straddles it. To overbid is to bid more than a hand or lot is worth, a misjudged risk.
annotation.definitionFit: To overbid is to bid beyond what is wise, having poorly estimated the risk.

entries.clue: Wine – cork removed – bravo! (4,4)

indicators.note: the letters are moved away from their places and rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: Someone cheers as the cork comes out of a bottle of wine.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cork removed' reads as uncorking the bottle, suggesting a deletion of CORK; instead 'removed' tells you to rearrange WINE and CORK together.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Nice work!' and 'Bravo!' are both cries of praise.

entries.clue: Tear and shatter (4)

blocks.note: verb: to rush along, tear down the road
verb: to smash to pieces, as hopes can be

annotation.walkthrough: Tear here rhymes with 'bear', to rush, not with 'beer'; dash as in dashing someone's hopes gives the second sense.
annotation.definitionFit: To dash is to tear along at speed, and also to smash or shatter.

entries.clue: Where a nest egg may be found to be at risk (3,2,1,4)

definitions.text: Where a nest egg may be found

blocks.clueFragment: Where a nest egg may be found
blocks.note: taken literally: a bird's egg in a nest sits out on a branch of a tree
the idiom for being in an exposed, unsupported position

annotation.surface: A saver's nest egg is in danger.
annotation.walkthrough: A nest egg here is literal: a bird's egg in a nest, which sits out on a limb of a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: Being out on a limb means being in an exposed, risky position.

entries.clue: Initially chatty, Everyman's accepted by company that's put up with one trying to amuse (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of 'chatty'
the company takes the other letters on, placing them after CO
in a down clue, putting something up reverses it so it reads upward

blocks.note: CO = company
first letter of chatty
the setter, Everyman, says 'I am' = I'M

annotation.surface: A talkative company tolerates the setter's attempts to be funny.
annotation.walkthrough: C and I'M are put up to read MIC, and CO accepts them to make COMIC. The setter's own name standing for I'M is a common trick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain noun sense: a comic is a stand-up or comedian, whose job is getting laughs.

entries.clue: Quiet, because around the French (7)

indicators.note: the first word goes around the second

blocks.note: since = because
le = 'the' in French

annotation.surface: Someone is quiet because of the French.
annotation.walkthrough: The comma splits the definition off at the front; 'because' is not a link word here but a synonym that supplies letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Silence as a noun or command means quiet.

entries.clue: One-time occupier of dark room who's been relatively immature? (4,9)

definitions.note: the second definition describes the person: 'one who's been relatively immature'

blocks.note: late = former; a developer of photographs worked in a darkroom
someone who grows up more slowly than their peers

annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is jokey: a photographic developer once worked in a darkroom, so a 'late' (former) developer occupied one.
annotation.definitionFit: A late developer is someone slow to mature; a former darkroom worker is literally a late developer.

entries.clue: When graduates trained hoi polloi (5,8)

indicators.note: training shapes something into a new form, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 13 letters

annotation.surface: Graduates, once trained, became the common people.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics mark hoi polloi as a foreign phrase: Greek for 'the many', the common people.
annotation.definitionFit: The great unwashed is a scornful name for the masses, the hoi polloi.

entries.clue: Somewhere in Bolivia, personal assistant coming back with illuminating insights (7)

indicators.note: the letters return, reading from right to left

blocks.note: Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia
PA = personal assistant

annotation.surface: A personal assistant returns from a trip to Bolivia full of bright ideas.
annotation.walkthrough: SUCRE + PA is reversed as a whole to read APERCUS. An aperçu is a French-derived word for a quick insight.
annotation.definitionFit: Aperçus are brief, illuminating insights or glimpses.

entries.clue: One that'll take a drink, or one that's had too many? (7)

blocks.note: a flat-bottomed drinking glass holds a drink
whimsical: a drunk falls over, so is one who tumbles

annotation.walkthrough: A tumbler is a glass that holds a drink; someone who has had too many drinks tumbles over, so they are a tumbler too.
annotation.definitionFit: A tumbler holds a drink, and a drunk who keeps falling over is humorously a tumbler.

entries.clue: Joint enterprise finally getting large yield (5)

indicators.note: take the final letter of 'enterprise'

blocks.note: last letter of enterprise
L = large
to bow is to yield or submit

annotation.surface: A joint business venture is finally paying off handsomely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Joint enterprise' reads as a single phrase, a joint venture, but Joint is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the elbow is one particular joint, the hinge between upper arm and forearm.

entries.clue: A nasty aquatic creature. One's nature? Drowning animals, primarily! (8)

definitions.text: A nasty aquatic creature. One's nature? Drowning animals, primarily!

indicators.note: take the first letter of each word before it

blocks.clueFragment: A nasty aquatic creature. One's nature? Drowning animals
blocks.note: first letters of A Nasty Aquatic Creature One's Nature Drowning Animals

annotation.surface: A description of a vicious water beast whose nature is to drown its prey.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the anaconda, which kills by squeezing and drowning prey in water, while its first letters spell the name.
annotation.definitionFit: The anaconda is a huge South American water snake that often drowns the animals it catches.

entries.clue: Then where might I have packed those items? (2,4,4)

definitions.text: where might I have packed those items?

blocks.note: the phrase meaning 'if so, then'

blocks.clueFragment: where might I have packed those items?
blocks.note: read literally: inside that suitcase

annotation.surface: Someone asks where they could have packed their things.
annotation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'in that case' is a suitcase where the items were packed; as a phrase it means 'then'.
annotation.definitionFit: 'In that case' and 'then' both mean 'if so'.

entries.clue: Underlying – put another way, having long-term effect (10)

definitions.note: the answer is an adverb; the definition reads as an adjective phrase, loosely 'in a way having long-term effect'

indicators.note: the word is expressed in a different arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters

annotation.surface: A remark about an underlying cause whose effect lasts a long time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put another way' reads as 'in other words', but here it rearranges the letters of Underlying.
annotation.definitionFit: Enduringly means in a lasting way, with long-term effect.

entries.clue: Ribbons arranged, we're told, for fancy man (4)

indicators.note: we hear it, so it is a sound-alike

blocks.note: ribbons arranged into loops make a bow

annotation.surface: Someone ties ribbons prettily for a dashing boyfriend.
annotation.walkthrough: A fancy man is a boyfriend or lover, and beau is the French-derived word for one.
annotation.definitionFit: A beau is a woman's admirer or lover, a fancy man.

entries.clue: Being twisted, I'll abase Catholic monarch (8)

indicators.note: the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

annotation.surface: A twisted plotter vows to humiliate a Catholic king or queen.
annotation.walkthrough: Isabella I of Castile, with her husband Ferdinand, was one of the 'Catholic Monarchs' of Spain.
annotation.definitionFit: Isabella of Castile was given the title Catholic Monarch by the Pope.

entries.clue: Most common Scrabble tiles gathered, bringing comfort (4)

indicators.note: one set of tiles gathers the other inside it

blocks.note: E is the most common tile in Scrabble, so Es = E, E
A is the next most common, so As

annotation.surface: Picking up a rack of Es and As makes a Scrabble player relax.
annotation.walkthrough: E(AS)E: the Es gather the As between them. E has twelve tiles in an English Scrabble set and A nine, the two commonest letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to live in ease is to live in comfort, free of hardship.

entries.clue: Armpit often seen in leisurewear (7)

blocks.note: whimsical: an armpit is a thing that sweats
a knitted jumper, a staple of casual clothes

annotation.walkthrough: The first sense is playful: an armpit is something that sweats, so a sweater. The second is the jumper worn casually.
annotation.definitionFit: A sweater is a knitted top common in casual clothing, and literally anything that sweats.

entries.clue: Tries to get a ride from ship's company: it's torturous! (10)

definitions.note: the definition is a phrase describing the device: 'it's a torturous thing'

blocks.note: a hitchhiker thumbs a lift
a ship's company is its crew

annotation.surface: A hitchhiker trying to get a lift from a ship's crew finds it agonising.
annotation.walkthrough: A thumbscrew is a torture device that crushes the thumbs.
annotation.definitionFit: The thumbscrew was an instrument of torture, so it is literally torturous.

entries.clue: Arranging – in a bad way – support for masts and sails (7)

blocks.note: fixing a result dishonestly, as with a crooked vote
a ship's ropes, chains and wires

annotation.walkthrough: Rigging an election or a match is arranging it dishonestly; a ship's rigging is its ropes and wires.
annotation.definitionFit: Rigging means fixing a result dishonestly, and the system of ropes supporting masts and sails.

entries.clue: Displays gluttony having consumed tea before end of cricketing encounters (8)

indicators.note: the outer word swallows the inner one
the inserted piece goes just before the last letter

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled at the batsman
to take tea is to eat

annotation.surface: Players stuff themselves at the tea break near the end of a cricket match.
annotation.walkthrough: Tea is the afternoon break in a cricket match, so the surface is a cricket scene; the insertion point is fixed by 'before end', not the middle.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone who overeats is showing gluttony.

entries.clue: Feeling fed up with starters of escargots nightly, night in Paris cut short (5)

indicators.note: take the first letters of the next two words
something cut short loses its end, so the final T of NUIT is trimmed off

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
nuit is French for night; cut short to NUI

annotation.surface: A diner in Paris grows sick of snails served every night.
annotation.walkthrough: The italics mark 'in Paris' as the French cue. Ennui is itself a French loan word for weary boredom.
annotation.definitionFit: A French loan word for weary dissatisfaction, the mood of someone fed up with everything.

entries.clue: Fraudulent old girl taking public transport? (5)

indicators.note: the old girl takes the bus, so she goes inside it

blocks.note: a bus is public transport
OG = old girl

annotation.surface: A dodgy old woman catches the bus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking' usually means the first piece swallows the next; here she takes the bus in the travelling sense, so she ends up inside it. OG for old girl is also a British school term for a former pupil.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a bogus claim or banknote is counterfeit, made to deceive.

entries.clue: Somewhat nouveau – that includes Iris (4)

definitions.note: the definition is a relative clause: '(the part) that includes the iris'

indicators.note: only some of the word is used

blocks.note: the four middle letters of the word, dropping the first two and the last

annotation.surface: A little bit of nouveau style, including someone called Iris.
annotation.walkthrough: Iris is capitalised to look like a woman's name; it is the coloured part of the eye.
annotation.definitionFit: The uvea is the middle layer of the eye, made up of the iris, ciliary body and choroid.

entries.clue: Ecstasy tablets and C illegally acquired at source in Baltic state (7)

first letter

entries.clue: Uranium record held by source of wine: cunning! (7)

indicators.note: the first pieces are held inside the later one

blocks.note: wine comes from the vine
U = uranium
LP = long-playing record

annotation.surface: A uranium record is kept by a wine source, a crafty move.
annotation.walkthrough: V(ULP)INE. Vulpine means fox-like, and foxes are proverbially cunning.
annotation.definitionFit: Vulpine means like a fox, so crafty or cunning.

entries.clue: Proved highly amusing? (6,1,5)

blocks.note: the surface reads 'turned out to be very'; the setter means dough that has proved, risen up high, so RAISED
the surface reads a plain adjective; the setter means producing A LAUGH

annotation.walkthrough: Bakers say dough 'proves' when it rises before baking, and that sense of proved is the seam the question mark flags.
annotation.definitionFit: To raise a laugh is to make people laugh, to prove amusing.
